title: Co-occurring maternal emotional well-being and lifestyle profiles from pregnancy to postpartum and offspring developmental outcomes: A prospective cohort study.
authors: Chakranon P, Huang JP, Au HK, Lin CL, Chen YY, Mao SP, Kim P, Taya DA
abstract: Maternal emotional well-being and lifestyle behaviors co-occur during the perinatal period, yet most studies examine them separately. Using data collected since 2019 from the Longitudinal Examination Across Prenatal and Postpartum Health in Taiwan, a prospective cohort of 539 mother-child dyads, we assessed maternal depressive symptoms, eudaimonic well-being, fruit and vegetable intake, physical activity, and sleep duration from early pregnancy to 2 years postpartum. Group-based multi-trajectory modeling identified co-occurring maternal profiles. Birth weight was analyzed with multiple linear regression, and repeated measures of child attention, aggression, internalizing symptoms, and suspected language delay (ages 2-5 years) with generalized estimating equations, adjusting for covariates. Four perinatal profiles emerged: holistic flourishing (perinatal-HF), lower behavioral engagement, higher well-being (perinatal-LBE-HWB), higher behavioral engagement, lower well-being (perinatal-HBE-LWB), and high-risk (perinatal-HR). Relative to perinatal-HF, the perinatal-HR profile was associated with higher attention problems (aβ = 0.75; 95% CI, 0.35-1.16), aggression (aβ = 5.34; 95% CI, 3.85-6.83), internalizing problems (aβ = 5.65; 95% CI, 4.12-7.19), and suspected language delay (AOR = 2.38; 95% CI, 1.23-4.61). Notably, mothers with preserved emotional well-being but lower behavioral engagement showed comparatively favorable child outcomes. In contrast, mothers with lower emotional well-being showed elevated child behavioral risk despite healthier behaviors. Distinct co-occurring maternal profiles were differentially associated with offspring development, supporting multidomain perinatal screening and interventions that prioritize maternal emotional well-being.

title: The application progress of detection technology for Bacillus cereus in food: Challenges, innovations and future prospects.
authors: Zhang Y, Zhang X, Zheng H, Wang H, Yu M, Jia W, Jia Z, Cui J
abstract: Food safety is a key issue of global public health. As a foodborne pathogen - Bacillus cereus (B. cereus), it is widely distributed in nature and can cause diseases in both humans and animals. The rapid detection of B. cereus is of great significance for the prevention and control of such diseases. This article provides a detailed overview of the development of B. cereus detection techniques in food, transitioning from traditional methods to a series of current technologies such as immunology, molecular biology and MALDI-TOF-MS. The principles, advantages and disadvantages of various detection techniques, as well as their application progress, were outlined. Furthermore, the application and advantages of combining different techniques in the detection of B. cereus in food were demonstrated. The CRISPR/Cas system possesses the characteristics of high specificity, high sensitivity and ease of operation, and shows great potential in the field of foodborne pathogen detection. This article also explains that the combination of CRISPR/Cas technology with RPA, LFA and AI technologies can further enhance the detection rate and accuracy. The aforementioned technology can enable the early detection and prevention of B. cereus in food, ensuring food safety and preventing the outbreak of foodborne diseases. This article has certain reference value in the research on the detection techniques of B. cereus and other foodborne pathogens in food, and provides strong support for safeguarding food safety and maintaining human health.

title: Artificial Intelligence in suicide prevention: promise, peril, and clinical implications for clinical practice.
authors: Nobile B, Courtet P
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into psychiatry is progressing rapidly, with promising yet underexplored applications in suicide prevention. While most existing studies have focused on suicide risk prediction, AI could be applied more broadly across the suicide prevention continuum. This review explores AI's potential in improving the detection of suicidal ideation (SI), enhancing clinician training, and expanding patient access to psychotherapeutic support. Studies suggest that AI models may identify SI more sensitively than clinicians by detecting subtle linguistic or semantic cues. Furthermore, AI-based virtual patients have been shown to improve clinicians' confidence and accuracy in suicide risk assessments, particularly when used alongside traditional training methods. On the patient side, CBT-inspired AI tools offer scalable, on-demand support, but most remain unregulated and clinically unvalidated. Despite their perceived empathy and availability, such tools pose ethical and clinical risks. Many patients use AI tools without professional guidance, a trend clinicians often underestimate. This disconnect calls for urgent regulatory oversight and professional engagement. Without clear clinical validation, AI-based tools may evolve outside medical frameworks, exposing vulnerable individuals to preventable harm. Psychiatry must not only adapt but also lead, ensuring that innovation is harnessed responsibly to serve patients with empathy, safety, and scientific rigor.

title: Postoperative infections after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass - incidence, performance of diagnostic procedures, and predictive factors.
authors: Erixon C, Johannesson E, Dardashti A, Melhammar L, Nilsson J, Thelaus L, Linder A, Zindovic I
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Cardiac surgery using cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) induces a systemic inflammatory response that affects common inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein (CRP), white blood cell count (WBC), and body temperature, complicating postoperative diagnosis of infections. The objective of this study was to assess the incidence of postoperative infections and evaluate the performance of clinically used biomarkers. DESIGN: This was a bidirectional cohort study including patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB between 1st of February 2020 and 22nd of September 2021. Patients with postoperative infection were compared to patients without. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of postoperative infections. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluated the diagnostic ability of current biomarkers to detect infection. RESULTS: A total of 1,222 patients were included. The incidence of postoperative infections (during hospitalisation and/or late infection) was 17.3%. Patients with postoperative infection had more comorbidities, underwent more complex procedures, and had higher mortality (90-day mortality 3.8% vs 1.5%, p = 0.045; 1-year mortality 5.7% vs 2.7%, p = 0.032). CRP, WBC, and temperature performed poorly in detecting postoperative infection, although peak CRP (OR 1.069, p < 0.001) and peak temperature (OR 2.408, p = 0.005) were independent predictors of postoperative infection. Peak temperature occurred on postoperative day 5 in infected patients versus day 2 in those without infection. CONCLUSION: Postoperative infections following cardiac surgery with CPB remain common and are associated with increased postoperative complications and mortality. Common inflammatory biomarkers perform poorly in detecting infection. Improved diagnostic tools are needed to facilitate early detection and treatment.

title: Aptamer-functionalized EGCG nanocarrier for neutrophil-targeted AKBA delivery promotes anxiety-related fracture healing.
authors: Ouyang L, Zhang Y, Liao J, Zhang Z, He X, Lin Z, Tao R, Xie X
abstract: Anxiety is clinically associated with impaired fracture healing, but the underlying immunological mechanism remains unclear, and no targeted therapy is available. In a mouse model of chronic restraint stress (CRS)-induced anxiety with femoral fracture, we observed expansion of TGFβ1+CCR5+ double-positive neutrophils in the bone marrow. These neutrophils inhibited osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) via TGFβ1 secretion, while BMSC-derived CCL5 reciprocally promoted neutrophil activation, forming a detrimental feedback that disrupted fracture repair. Mechanistically, CRS activated the NF-κB-CCR5 axis to upregulate CCR5 and sustain this neutrophil subset. We found that acetyl-11-keto-β-boswellic acid (AKBA) directly bound YAP1, relieved YAP1-mediated suppression of ubiquitin-specific peptidase 31 (USP31), and consequently inhibited NF-κB phosphorylation and CCR5 expression, reducing the pathogenic neutrophil population and restoring BMSCs' osteogenic function. In order to overcome the problems of poor solubility, low bioavailability and tissue non-selectivity of AKBA, we developed a NIMP-R14 aptamer-modified epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG)-coated nanocarrier (AKBA@E-N), which can achieve enhanced uptake and local retention of neutrophils in the acidic microenvironment of the fracture site. In vivo, AKBA@E-N significantly accelerated fracture healing compared with free AKBA. This study reveals a neutrophil-mediated mechanism linking stress to impaired bone repair and provides a targeted nanotherapeutic strategy.

title: Neuroimaging Biomarkers for Brain Disorder Diagnosis Using Advanced Learning Techniques.
authors: Ion IA, Chira C
abstract: Mental illness is becoming increasingly common in everyday life, affecting a growing number of people. Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) is an effective technique for detecting mental disorders. Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) analyses spontaneous low-frequency oscillations in the Blood Oxygen Level Dependent signal to examine the functional architecture of the brain. fMRI and rs-fMRI data processing contribute to mapping neural activity in specific brain regions, enabling accurate localization of cognitive functions and improving our understanding of Functional Connectivity and interactions among brain regions. This paper focuses on the use of Machine Learning and Deep Learning techniques for fMRI analysis to identify brain features that may be associated with Bipolar Disorder (BD) and Alzheimer's Disease (AD). The first step in the proposed approach is the preprocessing of fMRI and rs-fMRI data using two distinct methods: the first combines Statistical Parametric Mapping and the CONN toolbox for improved results, and the second focuses on the MELODIC software. The proposed approach begins with fMRI and rs-fMRI preprocessing using two pipelines: one integrating Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) with the CONN toolbox and another based on the MELODIC framework. The aim is to evaluate how preprocessing choices affect functional connectivity representations and classification performance when combined with classical Machine Learning (ML) methods, namely Support Vector Machines and Random Forests, and the Deep Learning (DL) model AlexNet. Given the altered brain connectivity patterns observed in Bipolar Disorder and Alzheimer's Disease, these methods are employed to assess preprocessing-learning interactions across both disorders. Experimental results emphasize that Connbox-SPM preprocessing combined with AlexNet yields the best results for both mental disorders, with Bipolar Disorder reporting 78.2% accuracy and AD achieving 82.4% accuracy.

title: Influence of perineal tears and body image disturbance on postpartum sexual quality of life: a cross-sectional study.
authors: Fillion D, Ruffolo AF, Verlet N, Martin C, Garabedian C, Rubod C, Kerbage Y, Cosson M
journal: Journal of psychosomatic obstetrics and gynaecology
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether perineal injury severity independently determines postpartum sexual quality of life (SQoL) is unclear. This study evaluated perineal tears and body image as determinants of SQoL and sexual resumption timing. METHODS: A total of 173 women (2-24 months postpartum, vaginal delivery) completed an online questionnaire including the SQoL-F and Body Image Scale (BIS). Women with perineal tear/episiotomy (PT/E; n = 118) were compared with those with an intact perineum (n = 51) using multivariate regression. RESULTS: SQoL-F scores were similar between groups (71.1 ± 23.3 vs 76.9 ± 24.0; p = 0.10), though PT/E delayed sexual resumption (p = 0.04). On multivariate analysis, SQoL-F was independently associated with dyspareunia (β = -10.96; p < 0.001), body image disturbance (β = -0.93; p < 0.001), and pre-pregnancy sexual satisfaction (β = +4.99; p = 0.001), but not tear type. Delayed resumption was independently associated with OASI (OR = 7.02; p = 0.02), first/second-degree tears (OR = 2.20; p = 0.04), and lower pre-pregnancy relationship satisfaction (OR = 0.50; p = 0.048). CONCLUSIONS: Postpartum SQoL is primarily determined by dyspareunia and body image disturbance rather than perineal tear severity. OASI carries a substantial risk of delayed sexual resumption, warranting dedicated postpartum counseling.

title: "Sailing Two Boats" the fragmented identity of working women and the hidden labor of infertility: a qualitative analysis.
authors: Dhar S, Poojari VG, Adiga P, Mundkur A, Tomar A, Kumar P
journal: Journal of psychosomatic obstetrics and gynaecology
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To explore how professional women undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART) experience and manage conflicts between treatment demands and professional identity; and to identify ways healthcare professionals can support them. METHODS: Following COREQ guidelines, semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with 18 professional women undergoing ART in a tertiary care hospital. Reflexive Thematic Analysis bolstered by interdisciplinary investigator triangulation (clinical and basic science) ensured thematic confirmability. RESULTS: Analysis revealed Gendered Occupational Asymmetry (female occupational burden regardless of clinical aetiology), the Insider Paradox (the role reversal for healthcare professionals) and the Workplace Panopticon (constant self-surveillance to preserve professional authority). Interestingly, work simultaneously often acted as a Sanctuary of Competence, providing psychological respite. Finally, narratives exposed an Existential Rumination (mourning past personal-professional decisions) and permanent temporal career stalling. These themes were further mapped onto a 'A Day in the Life' structural framework to illustrate compounding daily burdens. CONCLUSIONS: Current clinical lifestyle directives inadequately account for the rigid psycho-socioeconomic structures governing professional women. Based on identified themes, we propose targeted measures for healthcare professionals to deliver patient-centric care by integrating occupational awareness and identity-sensitive counselling into routine ART practice, thereby potentially reducing distress and improving treatment experience.

title: Hypoxia-associated birth complications and offspring childhood internalizing, externalizing, and adolescent depression symptoms.
authors: Davies NL, Smith EC, Pike MR, Cunningham R, Cohn BA, Krigbaum NY, Cirillo P, Alloy LB
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Hypoxia-associated birth complications (termed fetal hypoxia, herein) have been linked with increased offspring schizophrenia, autism spectrum disorder, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, all comorbid with depression. The current study examined the contribution of fetal hypoxia exposure to adolescent depression symptoms through childhood internalizing and externalizing symptom pathways. METHODS: Included mother-offspring dyads (N = 1679) were drawn from a subset of the Child Health and Development Studies (CHDS). Participants were part of two follow-up studies during childhood (ages 9 to 11) and adolescence (ages 15 to 19). Fetal hypoxia exposure was assessed prospectively from pregnancy and birth medical visits. Childhood internalizing and externalizing symptoms were assessed through questionnaires completed by mothers, and adolescent depressive symptoms were assessed via offspring self-report. RESULTS: Exposure to fetal hypoxia significantly increased childhood internalizing symptoms, which were subsequently linked to heightened adolescent depression symptoms. Fetal hypoxia showed no significant direct association with adolescent depression and was not associated with childhood externalizing symptoms. CONCLUSION: Findings indicate that fetal hypoxia is linked to offspring childhood internalizing symptoms, which in turn, increased risk for adolescent depression symptoms. These findings add to preclinical and preliminary human evidence linking fetal hypoxia to offspring depression.

title: Mitigation of ER stress improves bovine in vitro embryo development and pregnancy rates.
authors: Souza de Aguiar MH, da Costa DCA, Manenti NP, Agostini Xavier L, Lemos do Prado Welter N, Fontana Goetten A, Barreta MH, Gutierrez K
abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress compromises cellular homeostasis in multiple cell types, gametes and early embryos are particularly susceptible, with negative consequences for developmental competence. This study investigated the effects of ER stress and its attenuation by TUDCA at specific developmental stages of bovine embryos and evaluated ER stress-modulating compounds in a commercially in vitro embryo production (IVEP) system. To induce ER stress, embryos were exposed to tunicamycin (TN; 0.1, 1, and 10 ng/mL) during in vitro culture (IVC). Stage-specific sensitivity to ER stress was assessed by treating embryos 1 ng/mL TN during periods associated with embryonic genome activation (EGA): pre-EGA (days 1-3), EGA (days 3-5), and post-EGA (days 5-7). The ability of the bile acid tauroursodeoxycholic acid (TUDCA) to alleviate ER stress was then examined. Embryos received combined TN and TUDCA treatments either throughout culture or specifically during EGA, and outcomes were compared with TN alone. Finally, TUDCA supplementation was tested under commercial IVEP conditions. TN at 1 and 10 ng/ml dose-dependently reduced embryo development during in vitro culture (Days 1-7). Embryo development and total cell number were also decreased by 1 ng/ml TN during EGA (Days 3-5). TUDCA supplementation (100 μM) increased total cell number and the proportion of expanded blastocysts compared to controls and effectively mitigated TN-induced damage. In commercial IVEP, TUDCA supplementation increased blastocyst yield by ∼11% in beef cattle and improved pregnancy rates by 24.1% in dairy cattle. These results highlight the importance of ER stress during key embryo developmental stages and support the use of TUDCA as a beneficial supplement to enhance outcomes in commercial bovine IVEP systems.

title: Markers of pregnancy loss in Holstein heifers: insights from cervical interferon-stimulated gene mRNA, pregnancy-associated glycoproteins, and progesterone concentrations.
authors: Vivián R, de Brun V, Naya H, Gil J, Meikle A
abstract: Pregnancy loss during the first month of gestation remains a major limitation to reproductive efficiency in dairy cattle, yet the biological stage at which losses occur after the onset of conceptus-derived signaling remains poorly understood in nulliparous heifers. We evaluated cervical interferon-stimulated gene (ISG15, IFI44, OAS1, and RSAD2) expression, circulating progesterone (P4), and pregnancy-associated glycoprotein (PAG) concentrations in grazing Holstein heifers to characterize molecular and endocrine patterns associated with subsequent pregnancy outcomes. Cervical cytobrush samples and blood were collected on d16 after insemination from 103 heifers. Pregnancy status was determined by transrectal ultrasonography on d28 and d33, whereas PAG concentrations were measured on d28. Pregnancy outcomes were subsequently monitored until calving. Based on PAG concentrations, ultrasound determinations and ISG15 expression, heifers were classified as Nonpregnant (n = 10), Early pregnancy loss (EarlyPL; n = 38), Late pregnancy loss (LatePL; n = 7), or Pregnant (n = 48). Evidence of conceptus-derived interferon signaling was detected in 90.3% of inseminated heifers at d16, whereas only 53.4% were pregnant at d28 and 46.6% remained pregnant at d33, indicating that a substantial proportion of losses. All four ISGs were markedly upregulated in EarlyPL, LatePL, and Pregnant heifers relative to Nonpregnant heifers, confirming robust conceptus signaling in most inseminated animals. Among the genes evaluated, ISG15 exhibited the greatest dynamic range and uniquely differentiated all pregnancy outcome categories. P4 concentrations at d16 were similarly elevated in EarlyPL, LatePL, and Pregnant heifers relative to Nonpregnant heifers, indicating that many losses occurred despite adequate luteal support during maternal recognition. In contrast, PAG concentrations at d28 were lower in LatePL than Pregnant heifers, suggesting impaired progression through attachment and early placental development. Collectively, these findings indicate there although embryo signaling is detected and P4 concentrations are elevated on d16, a substantial proportion of losses occur before or shortly after the establishment of early placentation. Cervical ISG15 provided the greatest biological resolution across pregnancy outcomes, whereas PAG concentrations offered complementary insight into progression beyond maternal recognition, supporting a stage-specific model of pregnancy loss in which peri-attachment and early placental processes represent critical determinants of pregnancy maintenance.

Clinical Outcomes following invasive coronary angiography for patients with acute coronary syndromes pretreated with P2Y12 inhibitors and considered for urgent coronary artery bypass graft surgery.
authors: Lim CJ, Singh M, Sammut MA, Faizur Rahman ME, Parker WAE, Sadeque SAA, Storey RF
abstract: This retrospective single-centre observational study included 262 sequential patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) undergoing invasive coronary angiography (ICA) while receiving P2Y12 inhibitors and considered for coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); P2Y12 inhibitors (ticagrelor 91%, thienopyridine 9%) were stopped prior to CABG. The primary outcome was recurrent myocardial infarction or death following ICA and prior to revascularisation or decision for conservative management. 2 patients (0.8%) had recurrent MI and died following ICA and prior to planned CABG, demonstrating a small risk of MI and death in patients who have delays to CABG following ICA for ACS.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Gel Immersion Endoscopic Mucosal Resection With Submucosal Injection for Superficial Esophageal Squamous Neoplasms (With Video).
authors: Uda T, Urabe Y, Gurita T, Hatsushika Y, Masuda S, Sako Y, Nakamura T, Kamigaichi Y
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Gel immersion can provide a stable immersion environment during endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR). However, its application in superficial esophageal squamous lesions remains limited. In this study, we evaluated a gel immersion EMR (GI-EMR) technique in which submucosal injection was intentionally performed before snaring for selected small superficial esophageal squamous lesions. METHODS: This single-center, retrospective case series included consecutive patients who underwent GI-EMR with submucosal injection for superficial esophageal squamous lesions ≤15 mm in size between January and March 2026. The primary outcome was the histological en bloc resection rate, while secondary outcomes included technical success, endoscopic en bloc resection rate, procedure time, adverse events, and histopathological findings. RESULTS: GI-EMR with submucosal injection was attempted for 13 lesions, achieving a technical success rate of 92% (12/13). One procedure was discontinued because adequate lifting could not be achieved due to post-chemoradiotherapy scarring. The endoscopic and histological en bloc resection rates were both 85% (11/13) on an intention-to-treat basis. The median procedure time was 4.25 min (range, 2.0-11.0 min). No intraoperative or delayed perforation, post-procedure bleeding, or gel-related adverse events occurred. CONCLUSIONS: GI-EMR with submucosal injection was technically feasible for selected superficial esophageal squamous lesions ≤15 mm, with no serious procedure-related adverse events observed in this small case series. TRIAL REGISTRATION: N/A.

title: Flushing-Assisted Saline Immersion Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection in the Rectum: A Video-Based Feasibility Series.
authors: Matthews T, Landy J, Ban H, Toyonaga T, Suzuki N
abstract: Flushing endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is a refinement of saline immersion ESD in which energy-synchronized saline flushing from the knife tip is hypothesized to disperse micro-bubbles and facilitate more controlled coagulation at the tissue interface. We retrospectively evaluated the technical feasibility of this approach in 10 rectal procedures performed at a tertiary referral center. Complete procedural videos were reviewed to describe treated visible submucosal vessel burden, minor bleeding, episodes of transient loss of visualization, and hemostatic forceps use. En bloc and histologically margin-negative (R0) resection was achieved in all 10 cases, while curative endoscopic resection was achieved in nine cases (90%). No intraprocedural perforation, delayed bleeding, post-ESD coagulation syndrome, or unplanned repeat intervention occurred. Median lesion size was 55 mm (interquartile range, 40-69.5), median procedure duration was 102.5 min (100-167.5), and median treated visible vessel count was 21 (11.5-40.75), corresponding to 1.04 vessels/cm2 (0.64-1.74). Minor bleeding and transient loss of visualization occurred during procedures but were controlled endoscopically. Hemostatic forceps were required therapeutically for active bleeding from one vessel across the series, and no procedure required abandonment or conversion to surgery. These findings support the technical feasibility of rectal flushing-assisted saline immersion ESD. The video-derived hemostatic measures are descriptive and may provide candidate endpoints for future prospective comparative studies; they do not establish comparative efficacy, hemostatic benefit, or safety. Trial Registration: N/A.

title: Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Gallbladder Drainage as a Bridge to Surgery for Acute Cholecystitis: A Comparative Study.
authors: Nagai K, Fujita Y, Uechi H, Koyama Y, Tsujikawa S, Suzuki E, Tsujino S, Ishii K
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Gallbladder drainage is used for patients with acute cholecystitis (AC) who are unsuitable for emergency cholecystectomy. Percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage (PTGBD), endoscopic ultrasound-guided gallbladder drainage (EUS-GBD), and endoscopic transpapillary GBD (ETGBD) are used as bridge-to-surgery (BTS) approaches, but comparative data are limited. We compared clinical and perioperative outcomes among these strategies. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included 84 patients with AC who underwent GBD between January 2016 and January 2026 (PTGBD, n = 26; EUS-GBD, n = 39; ETGBD, n = 19). The primary endpoint was technical success. Secondary endpoints included clinical success, adverse events, recurrent cholecystitis, hospital stay, and surgical outcomes after BTS. RESULTS: Technical success rates were 100% in the PTGBD and EUS-GBD groups and 73.7% in the ETGBD group (p < 0.001). Clinical success rates were 92.3%, 100%, and 85.7%, respectively. Recurrent cholecystitis occurred in 7.7% of PTGBD cases and 14.3% of ETGBD cases, but not in EUS-GBD cases. Median hospital stay was the shortest in the EUS-GBD group (7 vs. 13.5 days for PTGBD and 9 days for ETGBD; p < 0.001). Among patients who proceeded to surgery, laparoscopic cholecystectomy was performed in 100%, 87.5%, and 75.0% of the EUS-GBD, PTGBD, and ETGBD groups, respectively (p = 0.041). CONCLUSIONS: All three approaches were feasible BTS strategies for AC. EUS-GBD achieved high technical and clinical success with acceptable safety. After successful BTS, surgical outcomes were broadly comparable among groups. Drainage strategy should be individualized based on patient conditions, anatomical feasibility, and circumstances. Trial Registration: N/A.

title: Physicians' perspectives of palliative care quality in nursing homes: a cross-sectional study.
authors: Sandsdalen T, Hov R, Sanaker H, Ødbehr LS
journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
abstract: BACKGROUND: Since physicians have primary responsibility for medical treatment, their perspectives of palliative care quality in nursing homes can provide important knowledge for service evaluation and enhancement in this context. However, few studies exist that include their perspectives. OBJECTIVES: The aim was to investigate physicians' perspectives of the quality of palliative care in Norwegian nursing homes. METHODS: A cross-sectional study conducted between November 2022 and December 2023, which included 77 nursing home physicians (response rate 43.5%) in Norway. Data were collected using a questionnaire comprising questions about demographic variables and perceptions of quality of care, as measured by the short form of the instrument Quality from the Patients' Perspective for Palliative Care (QPP-PC), adapted for healthcare personnel. Descriptive analyses and Wilcoxon signed rank tests were performed. RESULTS: Nursing home physicians scored subjective importance of the care significantly higher than their perception of the quality of actual care received in the two dimensions; medical-technical competence and sociocultural atmosphere and for nine out of the 24 items and three out of seven additional symptom-specific questions. A need for improvement was identified in care areas such as symptom relief for pain, depression and anxiety, existential care, understanding patients' perspective, waiting time, individualized care, cooperation, and continuity. CONCLUSION: The results show that provision of high-quality palliative care in nursing homes can be challenging and that the physicians identified several areas for improvement. The results can provide direction for future quality improvement. However, the findings need to be confirmed in a larger sample.

title: Exploring the Incidence of Immediate Suicidality Among Hand Surgery Clinic Patients.
authors: Hum R, Zama R, Xiong Y, Yohe GJ, Giladi AM
journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
abstract: PURPOSE: Depression is a known comorbidity in patients with chronic pain and musculoskeletal conditions, including specialty hand clinic patients. A subset experience active suicidal ideation or thoughts of self-harm at or around the time of their visit; however, epidemiological data are limited. We aimed to determine the prevalence of active suicidal ideation and hypothesized that hand surgery patients endorsing it would report greater pain, worse physical function, and greater socioeconomic disadvantage than those without suicidal ideation. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective review of patients presenting to our clinic from August 2022 to August 2023. They completed a Patient Health Questionnaire two-question (PHQ-2) screener; those scoring ≥3 completed the PHQ nine-question (PHQ-9). Active suicidal ideation ("high risk") was defined as a nonzero response to item 9 of the PHQ-9. Demographic, socioeconomic (including Area Deprivation Index), and patient-reported outcome data were collected. Chi-squared and t tests were used to compare high- and low-risk patients, and multivariable regression was used to assess adjusted associations between surgical status and follow-up patterns. RESULTS: Of the 7,023 new patients who completed the PHQ-2, 495 (7%) screened positive and completed the PHQ-9; 123 patients (1.8% of total) endorsed active suicidal ideation. Compared with low-risk patients, high-risk patients reported significantly higher pain, poorer global physical health, and worse upper extremity function, along with greater socioeconomic disadvantages, including higher Area Deprivation Index scores and more frequent transportation barriers. No significant differences occurred in surgical rates or follow-up utilization between high- and low-risk patients, including after stratification by procedure type. CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 1 in 50 new patients reported active suicidality, greater pain, worse physical function, and greater socioeconomic burden-differences that exceeded published minimal clinically important differences. Screening tools and targeted surgeon education may aid in early identification and guide opportunities for intervention and support. TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic IV.

title: Cold-induced transcriptomic responses are associated with strain-dependent Salmonella enterica persistence in refrigerated lettuce leaves.
authors: Rodríguez-Alvarez Y, González N, Araya MP, Moreno-Switt AI, Melotto M, Jacob C
abstract: Salmonella enterica is a leading cause of foodborne outbreaks linked to leafy greens. Refrigerated storage is a cornerstone of leafy-green safety, yet strain-level variation in the persistence of internalized S. enterica under these conditions remains poorly understood. Screening of eleven S. enterica strains revealed marked differences in their persistence within detached romaine lettuce leaves stored at 10 °C. Two isolates, belonging to serovars Montevideo and Newport, displaying contrasting persistence phenotypes were selected for detailed analysis, and these differences were confirmed at 4 °C. To investigate transcriptional responses associated with this variation, we profiled transcriptomic responses to cold stress in nutrient-rich medium by RNA-seq and evaluated post-cold recovery. Both isolates grew similarly at 28 °C but diverged at 4 °C, with the Montevideo strain maintaining higher growth capacity. Functional enrichment of KEGG pathways and Gene Ontology terms revealed shared repression of central metabolic and energy-producing pathways, coupled with induction of stress-response processes. Genes associated with general stress responses, cold-shock functions, and envelope integrity were more prominently represented among the induced responses of the Montevideo strain after cold exposure. These findings indicate that strain-dependent differences in Salmonella persistence during refrigerated lettuce storage are associated with distinct transcriptional responses to cold stress and post-cold recovery phenotypes observed in cultured bacteria. Consideration of strain-level variation may improve interpretation of pathogen persistence during leafy-green storage and inform future microbial risk assessments.

title: 3D printed Bouncy Bioglass enhances articular cartilage regeneration.
authors: Heyraud A, Tallia F, Al-Jabri T, De Mori A, Shi QE, Dos Santos DMM, Clark JN, Gupte C
abstract: Articular cartilage is an avascular tissue with limited intrinsic repair capacity, and untreated defects will deteriorate progressively over time. Lining the ends of bones, it plays a critical role in joint lubrication and shock absorption. Current surgical interventions, such as microfracture, typically result in the formation of mechanically inferior fibrocartilage. There remains a significant unmet clinical need for biomaterials that can support the regeneration of functional articular cartilage. We present a non-cytotoxic sol-gel hybrid scaffold, of composition silica/poly(tetrahydrofuran)/polycaprolactone (SiO2/PTHF/PCL-diCOOH), termed 'Bouncy Bioglass' to address that need. Our ovine model revealed that Bouncy Bioglass scaffolds with 250 μm channels stimulated hyaline cartilage regeneration. They outperformed scaffolds with 500 μm channel and microfracture alone, by improved integration and filling of the defect site with articular-like cartilage tissue. This tissue showed a significant increase in collagen type II and other primary components of healthy articular cartilage, compared to the tissue formed from the other two conditions. Our hybrid biomaterial, Bouncy Bioglass, enhances the regeneration of articular cartilage and may offer an 'off-the-shelf' synthetic implant option to treat localised articular defects and prevent their continued degeneration.

title: Nutrient availability and sodium pyruvate regulate the resuscitation of viable but nonculturable Staphylococcus aureus.
authors: Yu H, Ge R, Du J, Hua Y, Zhao F
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) can enter a viable but nonculturable (VBNC) state when induced by citric acid at 4 °C, posing hidden risks to food safety upon resuscitation. However, the effects of nutritional conditions and sodium pyruvate (SP) on this process remain unclear. This study demonstrates that 0.5 × TSB, TSB, 2 × TSB, and SP resuscitate VBNC cells following sigmoidal kinetics, with an efficacy ranking of SP > 2 × TSB > TSB > 0.5 × TSB. SP significantly accelerated resuscitation through enhanced early enzymatic activity, a transient increase in intracellular ROS levels, and rapid ATP accumulation, accompanied by dynamic nucleic acid fluctuations peaking at 10-12 h. Furthermore, proteomic profiling and targeted inhibition analyses revealed that DNA repair and cell wall biosynthesis are critically involved in initiating resuscitation, whereas signal transduction and respiratory metabolism primarily govern post-resuscitation growth. Practically, a 5-h or 10-h pre-resuscitation in 2 × TSB successfully detected VBNC S. aureus in high pressure processing-treated apple juice during 4 °C storage, which was undetectable via direct enumeration. These findings offer mechanistic insights into pathogen resuscitation and provide practical strategies for food safety risk assessment and detection.

title: Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Structural Optimization under Fluid-Structure Interaction.
authors: Narkhede A, Rivas E, Wang K
journal: Computer methods in applied mechanics and engineering
abstract: The design of structures and vehicles subject to fluid-structure interaction (FSI) often requires high-fidelity coupled analysis. While the design variables pertain to the structure, the computational cost is usually dominated by the fluid solver, making iterative optimization prohibitively expensive. This paper presents an adaptive multi-fidelity optimization method that combines high-fidelity FSI analysis with a lightweight surrogate for fluid-induced loads and a decision model that selects between surrogate and high-fidelity fluid evaluations. During optimization, results from completed FSI analyses are used to incrementally update a non-intrusive surrogate model based on nearest-neighbor search and radial interpolation. To maintain accuracy across varying geometries, a hybrid Lagrangian-Eulerian mapping function is developed to transfer fluid loads between structural designs. The evolution in surface orientation is handled through decomposition of the traction vectors in local orthonormal bases. An adaptive Gaussian process regression model is employed to predict surrogate error and quantify uncertainty, allowing risk-aware selection of when coupled analysis is required. As design evaluations cluster near the optimal solution, the accuracy of the surrogate model naturally improves, thereby reducing the reliance on high-fidelity fluid evaluations. This optimization framework treats the high-fidelity FSI model as the ground truth, instead of a pre-computed dataset. It requires no offline training, preserves the high-fidelity structural model in all design evaluations, and ensures that the final design is evaluated by high-fidelity FSI analysis. The fundamental idea is justified theoretically using a simplified model problem, which shows that the leading-order error is a monotonically increasing, concave, and bounded function of the fluid added mass. The framework is implemented using open-source software and demonstrated numerically through two benchmark examples. For shape optimization of a flexible panel under shock loading, results show an 80% reduction in computational cost while maintaining accuracy within 2.3% of fully high-fidelity FSI optimization.

title: Identification of Tex and the Phage Shock Protein YthA as putative FtsH substrates associated with the cell envelope stress response in Lactococcus cremoris.
authors: Rendueles C, Escobedo S, Campelo AB, Alonso-Fernández S, Rau MH, Gaspar P, Narberhaus F, Martínez B
abstract: As part of the Cell Envelope Stress (CES) response orchestrated by the two-component system CesSR in lactococci, the FtsH protease is expected to play a role in counteracting stress, as observed in other bacteria. However, neither its specific role nor its substrates have been identified in this genus. The primary objective of this study was therefore to elucidate the FtsH function in the context of CES. A Lactococcus cremoris NZ9000 ΔftsH exhibited an extended lag phase, increased salt and heat sensitivity and lysozyme resistance. However, only the salt and heat sensitive phenotype could be restored by complementation of the ftsH deletion. Whole-genome sequencing revealed putative compensatory mutations in ΔftsH, including genes encoding a transcriptional regulator and components of ABC transporters. Although awaiting experimental validation, these mutations may nevertheless underscore the broader physiological significance of FtsH in L. cremoris. Furthermore, a comparative proteomic analysis of L. cremoris NZ9000 ΔftsH under CES conditions identified putative FtsH substrates. In vivo degradation experiments demonstrated an extended half-life of the RNA-binding protein Tex and the Phage-Shock Protein YthA in a growth-phase dependent manner, thereby proposing these proteins as putative FtsH substrates in L. cremoris. While the specific function of Tex remains to be elucidated, the regulated degradation of YthA suggests that proteolysis may represent an additional regulatory layer within the lactococcal CES response.

title: Treat the patient, not the MRI: Lessons from low-dose radiotherapy for plantar fasciitis.
authors: Micke O, Kriz J, Mücke R, Seegenschmiedt MH
abstract: The recent study by Novo-Rigueiro et al. adds important prospective evidence for low-dose radiotherapy (LDRT) in refractory plantar fasciitis. After failure of conservative treatment and extracorporeal shock wave therapy, patients showed durable improvements in pain, function, and health-related quality of life, yet magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings correlated poorly with clinical response. This discrepancy deserves attention because structural imaging does not necessarily reflect therapeutic success. In benign radiotherapy, patient-reported outcomes, functional recovery, and quality of life should remain the primary measures of efficacy, with imaging as a complementary biomarker. This view is consistent with the recently published ASTRO-ESTRO-DEGRO-RANZCR Framework for radiation therapy in nonmalignant diseases, which emphasizes multidisciplinary care, modern radiotherapy techniques, and clinically meaningful outcomes. The study therefore reaches beyond plantar fasciitis. Future prospective studies, international registries, and guidelines should prioritize standardized patient-centered endpoints while integrating imaging into a translational framework rather than using radiological normalization as a surrogate for clinical benefit.

title: Persistence and epidemiological relevance of Salmonella enterica Newport in public-access waters from a central California coastal agricultural region.
authors: Carter MQ, Carychao D, Gorski L
abstract: Salmonella enterica Newport is one of the most common serotypes linked to fresh produce-associated salmonellosis outbreaks in the United States. In this study, we examined the genetic diversity and epidemiological relevance of 20 Newport strains recovered from Salinas Valley watersheds between 2012 and 2016. Multilocus Sequence Typing (MLST) identified two sequence types (STs), with ST118 representing 70% of isolates and ST45 comprising the remainder. Core-genome MLST (cgMLST) resolved 12 cgSTs, with cgST132506 being the most common. Phenotypic analyses revealed lineage-specific traits, including enhanced biofilm formation and reduced river-water survival in cgST132506 strains. Additionally, ST45 strains adhered significantly better to cantaloupe rind but produced less biofilm on glass surfaces compared with ST118 strains. Epidemiological relevance was assessed by examining matched strains in identified Single Nucleotide Polymorphism (SNP) clusters using the Pathogen Detection pipeline. Two strains were classified as persistent (>500 matches), six as intermediate (50-500), and twelve as transient (<50). Persistent and intermediate strains, considered strains of concern (SOCs), were genomically related to known outbreak strains and widely detected across the United States, including those linked to the 2012 cantaloupe-associated outbreak and the 2017 watermelon-associated outbreak. Although no significant difference in attachment to cantaloupe rind was observed between SOCs and transient strains, SOCs displayed greater river-water survival, while transient strains produced significantly more biofilm. Diverse Newport strains were isolated from the two watersheds examined, and multiple SOCs were recovered from three locations, highlighting the need for targeted investigations into contamination sources in these areas.

title: Persistence of hepatitis A virus in a hydroponic nutrient solution at different temperatures.
authors: Jerkovic E, Walters K, D'Souza DH
abstract: Controlled environment agriculture (CEA) enables year-round production of produce to meet growing consumer demands. However, prevention of microbial contamination is essential. This study assessed the persistence of hepatitis A virus (HAV) over 21 days at 4, 15, 20, and 25 °C in a hydroponic nutrient solution to understand cross-contamination risk. Two-hundred μL of HAV (∼6.5 log PFU/mL) was aseptically inoculated into 1.8 mL of a commercial hydroponic nutrient solution (pH 5.8) and stored at 4, 15, 20, or 25 °C (mimicking storage, transport, and cultivation conditions) for 21 days. Infectious viruses were recovered over time and quantified using plaque assays in duplicate. The obtained recovered virus data from triplicate experiments were statistically analyzed. Hepatitis A virus retained infectivity after 21 days with reductions ranging from 0.22 log PFU/mL to 3.34 log PFU/mL. Storage at 4 °C supported greatest viral persistence (D-value = 41.34 ± 4.06 days), compared to 15 °C (D-value = 9.23 ± 2.70 days), 20 °C (D-value = 6.31 ± 3.92 days) or 25 °C (D-value = 8.03 ± 0.22 days). These findings support the risk associated with the contamination of hydroponic nutrient solutions, as the temperature of the solution shows an impact on the persistence of HAV. Overall, this study emphasized the need for adequate precautions and implementation of control methods in CEA to reduce the risk of foodborne viral cross-contamination.

title: A new three-layer metapopulation networks model coupling online-offline social interactions with epidemic spread.
authors: Chen N, Huo L
abstract: The dissemination of epidemic-related information can effectively enhance public awareness of preventive measures and decrease infection risks. However, information dissemination through multiple channels, including both online and offline sources, and the dynamics of information dissemination across these channels are influenced by individual mobility. To address this gap, this study develops a three-layer metapopulation network coupled model that integrates online information dissemination, epidemic spreading, and offline information dissemination. The proposed model systematically investigates the patterns of information dissemination through both online and offline channels, as well as the epidemic reaction-diffusion process driven by individual migration. Furthermore, the social interactions dynamics of both information channels are influenced by migration, manifested as migrated individuals acquire offline information in destination patches and establish online connections with individuals residing there. Theoretical analysis using the Microscopic Markov Chain Approach (MMCA) derives epidemic thresholds, while Monte Carlo (MC) simulations validate the model and examine factors influencing propagation dynamics. Results indicate that migration enhances individuals' offline information acquisition, and accelerates cross-patch online information dissemination. Both online and offline information interactions exert inhibitory effects on epidemic spread, effectively increasing the infection threshold and reducing the outbreak scale. Furthermore, increasing the connectivity and dissemination rate of online information, particularly the information dissemination via weak relationships between patches, can effectively inhibit epidemic outbreaks. Notably, when the suppression effect of information on the epidemic is weak, population migration facilitates epidemic spread. In contrast, when the suppression effect is strong, migration-driven information dissemination significantly reduces the probability of infection, thereby further suppressing the outbreak.
